sources.title: Llama-3.2-1B original base checkpoint model card
sources.evidence: Identifies Meta, pretrained Llama 3.2, 1B (1.23B), text input/output, GQA, shared embeddings, 128K context, September 25, 2024 release and the custom Llama 3.2 license. Separates base and instruction-tuned evaluations.

sources.title: Llama 3.2 launch announcement, September 25, 2024
sources.evidence: Releases original BF16 pretrained and instruction-tuned 1B/3B models. Describes structured pruning from Llama 3.1 8B, followed by pretraining distillation using Llama 3.1 8B/70B logits, and on-device deployment.

sources.title: Meta model registry: exact Llama 3.2 1B base SKU
sources.evidence: The base-model entry maps to meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B, with width 2048, 16 layers, 32 attention heads, eight KV heads and vocabulary 128256. It is separate from Instruct and INT4 variants.

sources.title: Meta model registry: precision defaults and context lengths
sources.evidence: The default checkpoint precision is BF16. Llama 3.2 max_seq_length is 131072 except INT4 variants, which are 8192. The 1B base SKU belongs to the Llama 3.2 family.

sources.title: Meta Llama reference Transformer implementation
sources.evidence: Autoregressive causal Transformer blocks each execute dense attention and a single SwiGLU feed-forward network; no routed experts. Linear projections have no biases and RMSNorm has learned scales. Rotary frequencies and KV caches are generated runtime tensors.

sources.title: Llama 3.2 exact prompt formats
sources.evidence: Explicitly scopes zero-shot function calling to 1B/3B Instruct models. A separate section identifies Llama3.2-1B and Llama3.2-3B base models and documents ordinary completion formatting.

sources.title: Llama 3.2 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: Names the custom license and September 25, 2024 version release; covers trained weights and grants conditional use and redistribution rights.

sources.title: Current combined Llama 3.2 model card
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened on October 27, 2026. Meta’s combined model card explicitly lists 1B (1.23B) for original Llama 3.2 text models and shared embeddings. It describes pretrained and instruction-tuned releases; the later quantized section is separate. It has no separate active-parameter column. The combined card dates the later quantized update October 24, 2024; this does not replace the original base release date.

sources.title: Meta Llama 3.2 model and quantization documentation
sources.evidence: Explains that BF16 lightweight models shipped first; quantized versions were subsequent, Instruct-only releases with reduced 8K context.

sources.title: Original checkpoint configuration access attempt
sources.evidence: The unauthenticated configuration request returned HTTP 401 because model access is restricted. No gate bypass, weight download, or tensor-header retrieval was attempted.

sources.title: Zipf’s and Heaps’ Laws for Tokens and LLM-generated Texts, Table 3 and Sections 4.1–4.2
sources.publisher: Nikolay Mikhaylovskiy (NTR Labs / Tomsk State University), Findings of EMNLP 2025
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened and Table 3 visually checked on October 27, 2026. The Llama-3.2-1B row explicitly gives Params 1.23B and Active params 1.23B. Section 4.1 identifies the experiments as using base and original instruction-finetuned models with BitsAndBytes NF4 quantization, and Section 4.2 reports base-model results including Llama 1B. This is the author’s nominal comparison convention for the underlying model, not a Meta active-count disclosure or a tensor-level participation measurement.

sources.title: Exact original Llama-3.2-1B checkpoint README fresh access attempt
sources.evidence: Fresh unauthenticated raw README request on October 27, 2026 returned HTTP 401. The public model landing page was reopened, and Meta’s accessible combined GitHub model card supplies the current nominal total. No weights or tensor census were retrieved.

name.note: Normalizes the display name of the exact original pretrained checkpoint, without an Instruct or quantization suffix.

developer.note: The exact model card explicitly identifies Meta as developer.

family.note: The exact SKU is in the Llama 3.2 release family.

release_date.note: The original model card, dated launch and license agree on September 25. October 24 on the current combined GitHub card accompanies the later quantized release.

open_weights.note: The original BF16 weights were released for download under the custom license. Access is gated by license acceptance.

license.note: Supported short name for the Llama 3.2 Community License Agreement.

parameters_b.note: Meta’s freshly reopened model card explicitly reports 1B (1.23B), with shared embeddings, for the original pretrained and instruction-tuned text models. Retains the developer’s nominal total at its published precision; it is not an exact learned-tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Table 3 of Mikhaylovskiy’s original EMNLP study explicitly labels Llama-3.2-1B as 1.23B active. Sections 4.1–4.2 establish that the listed models include the original base checkpoint, evaluated using NF4 quantization. Records the author’s nominal active-count convention at its published precision; Meta does not separately disclose this figure, and the paper does not define component-level or exact per-token participation.

architecture.note: Dense causal Transformer with GQA and SwiGLU; 16 layers, width 2048, 32 query heads and eight KV heads. Shared input/output embeddings are explicitly stated in the card; pruning and distillation do not imply routed-expert sparsity.

context_window.note: Meta assigns the exact original BF16 base SKU 131072 tokens. The separate 8192-token limit applies only to later INT4 variants.

modalities.note: The exact 1B model is text-only; code is text output. Vision inputs belong to separate 11B/90B variants.

reasoning.note: No dedicated thinking/reasoning mode is disclosed for this base checkpoint. Ordinary benchmark reasoning or generated chain-of-thought does not establish that flag.

tool_call.note: Native function-calling documentation and tool-use evaluations explicitly concern Instruct models. The base completion section does not establish a native tool interface or an explicit absence, so the baseline false is cleared.

description.value: Pretrained multilingual Llama 3.2 text model with 1.23B parameters, shared embeddings and 128K context, developed through pruning and distillation.
description.note: Describes the original pretrained text model and its documented training method; does not transfer Instruct tool use, chat alignment or quantized-model limits.

patch.notes: Meta reports a nominal 1.23B total with shared embeddings. The 1.23B active count follows Mikhaylovskiy’s EMNLP 2025 Table 3 convention for the original base model; it is not a separate Meta disclosure or exact per-token tensor count. A dedicated reasoning mode remains undisclosed. Native function calling is documented for the Instruct sibling, not established for this base checkpoint. Original BF16 context is 131072; later INT4 Instruct context is 8192. The September 25, 2024 base release predates the October 24 quantized update.

summary: The fresh parameter re-audit retains Meta’s nominal 1.23B total and replaces the unresolved active count with the explicit 1.23B nominal active convention in Mikhaylovskiy’s original EMNLP 2025 Table 3. The exact Llama-3.2-1B row and base-model experimental context establish identity; NF4 is the study’s execution format. Meta’s card has no separate active count, and neither source establishes exact tensor-level participation. Fresh searches for active-count disclosures found no stronger Meta specification. All twelve non-parameter field assessments are preserved.
